newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. fund visited Japan to sell palladium - traders.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fund visited Japan to sell palladium - traders.

text.p: Officials of U.S.-based hedge fund Tiger Management, which is believed to hold a massive amount of palladium through speculative futures trade, visited Japan last week to sell the metal, traders said on Monday.
Tiger Management associate director Dwight Anderson and two other company officials held talks with some Japanese traders on possible sales of palladium, traders said.
It is not clear whether any trade houses signed contracts to buy supplies from the fund, they said.

Most traders who met with Tiger Management were not interested in buying the rare white metal as they had already signed contracts to buy platinum and palladium from Russia this year under long-term contracts, traders said.
Traders who met with Tiger Management officials said the U.S. fund had tried to persuade them into buying palladium on a long-term basis, saying that Russia would not be a stable supplier.

"The U.S. hedge fund told us that they hope to sell the metal over a long-term period rather than a short-term period. Their purpose in visiting Japan was to market PGMs," a trading house trader who met Tiger Management said.

Another trader said: "The fund insisted that Russia would not be able to supply PGMs in the future (for an unknown reason), but we decided we not want to buy from Tiger Management because recent high prices for palladium and concerns about the stability of supplies have seriously cut into Japan's demand."

A prolonged suspension of Russian PGM sales since the beginning of this year, along with a suspected attempt by U.S. funds to squeeze the market has pushed PGM prices up sharply and has caused an acute shortage in supplies.
Russia supplies 60 percent of world palladium and about 20 percent of platinum.
Spot platinum prices are up about 50 percent from the beginning of this year and palladium prices have doubled.

Tiger Management is believed to have accumulated 1.5 million ounces of palladium, roughly 20 percent of 1996 world demand. It is believed that the fund started buying palladium when prices were at around $135 per ounce.
The February Issue of "Institutional Investor" magazine said Tiger Management, run by Julian Robertson, had been buying tons of palladium recently.
"At some point -- I don't know when -- all these people are going to be asking, where are we going to get our palladium," the magazine quoted Robertson as saying. "And the only place will be us."
On Monday palladium was quoted at $203.00/207.00.
Traders said they were mystified by why the fund had not yet sold its metal supplies despite the surge in prices.
